item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":4,"rationale":"The President presently continues the Cuba national emergency, a self-executing legal-status consequence, while also assigning the Secretary discretionary rulemaking authority whose consequences would arise only upon later issuance; these materially different postures are combined in one sub-directive.","evidence":"hereby continue the national emergency with regard to Cuba as set forth above and authorize and direct the Secretary of Homeland Security"},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The President authorizes, but does not require, the Secretary to issue vessel-anchorage and movement regulations; any regulated legal consequence occurs only if the Secretary later exercises that discretion.","evidence":"The Secretary may make rules and regulations governing the anchorage and movement of any vessel"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The President grants the Secretary discretionary operational authority to inspect vessels and place guards; the segment neither presently applies those measures to a vessel nor mandates a specified later outcome.","evidence":"The Secretary is authorized, to the extent consistent with international law, to inspect any vessel"},{"segment_id":"4","code":4,"rationale":"This segment inseparably aggregates discretionary enforcement authority and executive-branch assistance and delegation provisions with a hortatory appeal to nonfederal officials, supersession of prior proclamation provisions, and a congressional-transmittal command, which carry materially different postures.","evidence":"I urge all State and local officials to cooperate with Federal authorities"}]}
